The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets (Finite, countably infinite, countable, uncountable) has a choice function.

Assume countable choice. Let $K_0,K_1\subset S^3$ be smooth oriented knots. A smooth oriented knot cobordism from $K_0$ to $K_1$ is a compact smooth properly embedded oriented surface $\Sigma\subset S^3\times[0,1]$ whose boundary is $(-K_0\times\{0\})\sqcup(K_1\times\{1\})$, with product collars at both ends. A **generic movie** for $\Sigma$ is obtained by choosing a generic projection of the slices $S^3\times\{t\}$ to the plane and a Morse height function on $\Sigma$, then recording the oriented link diagram at each regular level. Intermediate regular levels may be links with any finite number of components. After choosing the projection and height generically, the finitely many exceptional levels are isolated and distinct: between them the diagrams change by planar isotopy or one oriented Reidemeister move, and at them the surface height has one nondegenerate minimum (a birth), one nondegenerate maximum (a death), or one index-one critical point (a saddle band move). A movie includes its ordered list of frames and these elementary changes; no claim that two movies of the same cobordism are equivalent is part of this definition.

Assume countable choice. Fix $\infty\in S^3$, put $A=\{\infty\}\times[0,1]$, and identify its complement with $\mathbb R^3\times[0,1]$. Let $S_0,S_1$ be compact smooth oriented link cobordisms disjoint from $A$, with the same fixed boundary parametrizations and product collars. If they are ambient isotopic in $S^3\times[0,1]$ relative to those collars, then their comparison factors into finitely many ambient isotopies supported in the Euclidean complement and finitely many local sheet passages through $A$. Each sheet passage occurs at a regular surface-height point and gives the sweep-around move: in planar movies, a closing arc for a one-interval tangle travels over the tangle to the opposite side and returns underneath, or the inverse, retaining its orientation. All end collars remain fixed. No assertion that a sweep-around is generated by the fifteen Euclidean Carter–Saito moves, or that any homology map respects it, is made.

Assume countable choice. Let two finite generic planar movies represent compact smooth oriented surfaces in $\mathbb R^3\times[0,1]$, with the same parametrized boundary and product collars. If their embedded surfaces are ambient isotopic with compact support relative to those collars, then the two movies are related by a finite sequence of the fifteen Euclidean Carter–Saito local types, distant interchanges of disjoint elementary movie events, and planar isotopies. All orientations and omitted-coordinate crossing orders are retained. This statement concerns Euclidean isotopies; it supplies no sweep-around relation.

Use coordinates $(x,y,z,t)$ on Euclidean space-time, with projection $(x,y,z,t)\mapsto(x,y,t)$; $z$ records the crossing order. A local movie move replaces the movies on the two sides of an isolated value $\lambda=0$ in a one-parameter deformation of a projected surface, with the surface and its collars unchanged outside the indicated region. Coordinates and cutoffs are chosen so the two movies have identical boundary frames. The following list specifies the fifteen Carter–Saito types, with their usual numbering. Include both directions, reflections, all compatible strand orientations, and every crossing order allowed by distinct $z$-coordinates. The quadratic and higher-order formulas specify the local topological models; sufficiently small perturbations with the same nonzero derivative signs give the same type.

| Type | Local change of the movie |
|---|---|
| MM1, MM2 | A pair of inverse R1 events is created or removed. In regular-height source coordinates $(v,t)$ the projected curve has local form $(v^2,(t^2-\lambda)v+c v^3)$, $c\ne0$; the two signs of $c$ relative to the quadratic term give the two types. |
| MM3, MM4 | A pair of inverse R2 events is created or removed. After the two projected branches are made graphs, their normal difference is $x^2+t^2-\lambda$ or $x^2-t^2-\lambda$. |
| MM5 | A pair of inverse R3 events is created or removed. With the intersection of two strands continued as the reference point, the signed displacement of the third strand is $t^2-\lambda$. |
| MM6 | An R3 event passes an R2 event: at the projected triple point exactly two projected tangents become parallel, with nonzero quadratic contact and nonzero relative deformation velocity. |
| MM7 | An R2 event meets a branch endpoint of the double-curve locus of an R1 picture. In projected coordinates use $(v^2,tv+\lambda v^3+v^5)$; its double pairs have $r=v^2\ge0$ and $t=-\lambda r-r^2$, so a critical point of the double-curve height enters or leaves through $r=0$. |
| MM8 | A third strand passes the branch point of an R1 picture; superpose a transverse strand on the ordinary cusp unfolding and move its displacement across zero. |
| MM9 | Two R2 critical levels merge and disappear, or are created, at a cubic inflection of the double curve: the branch-difference model is $x^3+\lambda x-t$. |
| MM10 | Four sheets meet at one projected point, with distinct omitted heights. Resolving the quadruple point in the two deformation directions gives the tetrahedral pair of R3 movies. |
| MM11 | A cancelling pair of surface Morse critical points is born or dies. The surface-height model is $u^2+v^3-\lambda v$, allowing both signs of the nondegenerate square and time reversal. |
| MM12 | At an extremum of surface height the projection of its tangent plane has rank one. A local embedded model is $(u,uv+\lambda v,v,u^2+v^2)$; the two movies interchange the extremum with its adjacent R1 picture. |
| MM13 | The corresponding interaction at a saddle, with embedded model $(u,uv+\lambda v,v,u^2-v^2)$. |
| MM14 | A projected strand passes a surface minimum or maximum: superpose an independently displaced regular sheet on the extremum picture. |
| MM15 | The corresponding projected strand passage across a saddle band. |

A **distant interchange** exchanges the order of two elementary movie events with disjoint spatial supports, including Reidemeister events and Morse events; it is not restricted to two critical points of the smooth surface-height function. A planar isotopy of a whole movie and the insertion or removal of stationary frames do not count as additional local types. Sweep-around is a separate spherical operation, absent from this Euclidean list.

Let $D$ be a nonempty finite regular oriented link diagram in an oriented $3$-sphere, with finite crossing set $C(D)$. Fix a unit viewing normal $n$ and orient the projection plane $P$ so $(u,v)$ is positive exactly when $(n,u,v)$ is positive in the ambient $3$-space. At a crossing $c$, define its sign as the sign of $\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})$, where the two nonzero projected tangent vectors follow the oriented over- and under-strands. Let $n_+$ and $n_-$ be the numbers of positive and negative crossings.

Set $\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$, with $\deg(1)=1$ and $\deg(X)=-1$. Its unit, multiplication, counit, and comultiplication are
$$
\eta(1)=1,\qquad m(1\otimes1)=1,\quad m(1\otimes X)=m(X\otimes1)=X,\quad m(X\otimes X)=0,
$$
$$
\epsilon(1)=0,\quad\epsilon(X)=1,\qquad \Delta(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1,\quad\Delta(X)=X\otimes X.
$$
Thus $m$ and $\Delta$ have quantum degree $-1$, while $\eta$ and $\epsilon$ have degree $+1$.

Choose a total order $c_1<\cdots<c_n$ on $C(D)$. A resolution state is a function $v:C(D)\to\{0,1\}$; at $v(c)=0$ use the A-smoothing and at $v(c)=1$ use the B-smoothing from the Kauffman source chart. Write $|v|=\sum_c v(c)$, let $D_v$ be the crossingless resolution, and let $k(v)$ be its number of circles. Assign the state module $\mathcal A^{\otimes k(v)}$. For an edge $v\to v+e_j$ changing crossing $c_j$ from $0$ to $1$, use $m$ if the local smoothing merges two circles and $\Delta$ if it splits one circle, tensored with the identity on all other factors, and multiply this map by $(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}v(c_i)}$. The resulting direct sum has cohomological degree
$$i(v)=|v|-n_-$$
and the generator with circle labels $1$ or $X$ has quantum degree
$$j(v)=|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum_{\text{circle labels }a}\deg(a).$$
This defines the normalized integral Khovanov cube and its candidate degree-zero cochain differential; the assertion that the differential squares to zero is a separate lemma.

The Frobenius identity that controls a merge-split face is represented by the two equal composites below. The diagram records the maps only; the proof verifies the equality on the basis $\{1,X\}^{\otimes2}$ and does not rely on the drawing.

```tikzcd
\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A \arrow[r,"m"] \arrow[d,"\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id}"'] & \mathcal A \arrow[d,"\Delta"] \\
\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A \arrow[r,"\mathrm{id}\otimes m"'] & \mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A
```

Let an object be a finite disjoint union of smooth embedded circles in the oriented plane $\mathbb R^2$, including the empty union. A cobordism from $C_0$ to $C_1$ is a compact smooth orientable surface properly embedded in $\mathbb R^2\times[0,1]$, with boundary $C_0\times\{0\}\sqcup C_1\times\{1\}$, product collars at those boundaries, and no other boundary. Surfaces are identified up to ambient isotopy fixed on the boundary collars. Compose cobordisms by gluing along their common boundary circles; the identity of $C$ is $C\times[0,1]$, and disjoint union gives the monoidal product. Let $\mathsf{Cob}_3$ be this additive monoidal category before imposing local relations.

Take the free abelian group on these isotopy classes of cobordisms and quotient by the following local relations, which are required to hold inside every surrounding cobordism. A sphere component is zero (the S relation). Adding a disjoint torus component multiplies a cobordism by $2$ (the T relation). For four disjoint disk patches numbered $1,2,3,4$, write $S_{ij}$ for the surface obtained by deleting the interiors of patches $i,j$ and joining their boundary circles by an orientable tube; the four-tube relation is $S_{12}+S_{34}=S_{13}+S_{24}$. The resulting additive monoidal category is denoted $\mathsf{Cob}_{BN}$.

derivations.claim: By the assumed functoriality of $F$, gluing cobordisms is sent to composition of maps and disjoint union is sent to tensor product. Thus the only additional relations to check before factoring through the quotient are the three local relations in [F2].

A sphere is evaluated by $\epsilon\eta$, and $\epsilon(\eta(1))=\epsilon(1)=0$. A torus is evaluated by $\epsilon m\Delta\eta$; on the generator $1$, $\Delta(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1$, then $m\Delta(1)=2X$, and $\epsilon(2X)=2$. These are exactly the S and T relations, including when glued into any surrounding cobordism because the TQFT respects composition and tensor product.

In the four-tube relation, each side consists locally of two ways to attach one tube. Applying the TQFT to the local four-disk input $1$, either side gives
$$
X\otimes1\otimes1\otimes1+ 1\otimes X\otimes1\otimes1+ 1\otimes1\otimes X\otimes1+ 1\otimes1\otimes1\otimes X.
$$
This follows by applying $\Delta(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1$ at each tube attachment and $\epsilon(1)=0,\epsilon(X)=1$ at the two cut disks. The equality on the local input implies equality as maps: tensoring with identity maps and composing with the maps for the unchanged part of the surface preserves equality. Thus the four-tube relation is respected.

Every generating local relation of $\mathsf{Cob}_{BN}$ is respected by steps 1.2 and 1.3, while the Frobenius identities respect the isotopy and gluing presentation by step 1.1. Therefore the TQFT factors through the quotient defining $\mathsf{Cob}_{BN}$, as asserted.

Full-curve periodic-domain lattices and their sublattices generated by pairwise periodic domains transport bijectively by the swept annuli. The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets (Finite, countably infinite, countable, uncountable) has a choice function.

Assume countable choice and fix a generic movie $M$ of a smooth oriented surface cobordism $\Sigma$ from an oriented link $L_0$ to an oriented link $L_1$. For each regular frame $D$, let $Kh(D)$ be the normalized integral Khovanov homology group. The empty frame has the one-term complex $\mathbb Z$ in both gradings zero, using the empty resolution and the zero-fold tensor product. Associate to a birth the unit map $\eta:\mathbb Z\to\mathcal A$, $\eta(1)=1$; associate to a death the counit $\epsilon:\mathcal A\to\mathbb Z$, $\epsilon(1)=0,\epsilon(X)=1$; and associate to a saddle the multiplication $m:\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ when two resolution circles merge, or the comultiplication $\Delta:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A$ when one splits. Each local map is tensored with the identity on unaffected circles. Associate to planar isotopy the induced identification of the cube complexes. For Reidemeister moves, use the following fixed Bar-Natan constructions: the kink retractions $F_+=v-\Delta$, $G_+=e$, $F_-=u$, $G_-=w-m$; the two inverse-crossing strong retractions with degree-zero inclusion $(1,ut)^T$ and projection $(1,-se)$, with their specified reverse-order cube signs; and the third-move equivalences obtained by the explicit source- or target-cone retractions onto the common six-point residual complex. Use their specified inverses for the reversed moves. Insert these formal surface matrices into the fixed planar outside of the diagram, then apply the integral Frobenius cobordism functor. Normalize a state $v$ to cochain degree $|v|-n_-$ and quantum shift $|v|+n_+-2n_-$. Fix the local coordinate identifications and orientation cases once, with the Koszul crossing-order correction $(-1)^{v(a)v(b)}$ when crossings $a,b$ are interchanged. This definition fixes a movie; independence from changing the movie is not included in the definition.

It respects S, T and four-tube and therefore descends to the closed Bar-Natan quotient category.

Let $\mathsf{Cob}_3$ be the additive monoidal category of oriented cobordisms before the S, T, and four-tube relations are imposed, and let $\mathsf{Cob}_{BN}$ be its quotient by those relations. Suppose $F:\mathsf{Cob}_3\to\mathsf{GrAb}$ is a symmetric monoidal functor to graded abelian groups and homogeneous maps, with a circle sent to $\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$, a cup to $\eta(1)=1$, a cap to $\epsilon(1)=0,\epsilon(X)=1$, a merge pair of pants to $m$, and a split pair of pants to $\Delta(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1,\ \Delta(X)=X\otimes X$. Then every sphere component is sent to zero, every disjoint torus component acts by multiplication by $2$, and the two sides of the four-tube relation induce the same map. Therefore $F$ factors through an additive monoidal functor on $\mathsf{Cob}_{BN}$.

Use coordinates $(x,y,z,t)$ on Euclidean space-time, with projection $(x,y,z,t)\mapsto(x,y,t)$; $z$ records the crossing order. A local movie move replaces the movies on the two sides of an isolated value $\lambda=0$ in a one-parameter deformation of a projected surface, with the surface and its collars unchanged outside the indicated region. Coordinates and cutoffs are chosen so the two movies have identical boundary frames. The following list specifies the fifteen Carter–Saito types, with their usual numbering. Include both directions, reflections, all compatible strand orientations, and every crossing order allowed by distinct $z$-coordinates. The quadratic and higher-order formulas specify the local topological models; sufficiently small perturbations with the same nonzero derivative signs give the same type.

| Type | Local change of the movie |
|---|---|
| MM1, MM2 | A pair of inverse R1 events is created or removed. In regular-height source coordinates $(v,t)$ the projected curve has local form $(v^2,(t^2-\lambda)v+c v^3)$, $c\ne0$; the two signs of $c$ relative to the quadratic term give the two types. |
| MM3, MM4 | A pair of inverse R2 events is created or removed. After the two projected branches are made graphs, their normal difference is $x^2+t^2-\lambda$ or $x^2-t^2-\lambda$. |
| MM5 | A pair of inverse R3 events is created or removed. With the intersection of two strands continued as the reference point, the signed displacement of the third strand is $t^2-\lambda$. |
| MM6 | An R3 event passes an R2 event: at the projected triple point exactly two projected tangents become parallel, with nonzero quadratic contact and nonzero relative deformation velocity. |
| MM7 | An R2 event meets a branch endpoint of the double-curve locus of an R1 picture. In projected coordinates use $(v^2,tv+\lambda v^3+v^5)$; its double pairs have $r=v^2\ge0$ and $t=-\lambda r-r^2$, so a critical point of the double-curve height enters or leaves through $r=0$. |
| MM8 | A third strand passes the branch point of an R1 picture; superpose a transverse strand on the ordinary cusp unfolding and move its displacement across zero. |
| MM9 | Two R2 critical levels merge and disappear, or are created, at a cubic inflection of the double curve: the branch-difference model is $x^3+\lambda x-t$. |
| MM10 | Four sheets meet at one projected point, with distinct omitted heights. Resolving the quadruple point in the two deformation directions gives the tetrahedral pair of R3 movies. |
| MM11 | A cancelling pair of surface Morse critical points is born or dies. The surface-height model is $u^2+v^3-\lambda v$, allowing both signs of the nondegenerate square and time reversal. |
| MM12 | At an extremum of surface height the projection of its tangent plane has rank one. A local embedded model is $(u,uv+\lambda v,v,u^2+v^2)$; the two movies interchange the extremum with its adjacent R1 picture. |
| MM13 | The corresponding interaction at a saddle, with embedded model $(u,uv+\lambda v,v,u^2-v^2)$. |
| MM14 | A projected strand passes a surface minimum or maximum: superpose an independently displaced regular sheet on the extremum picture. |
| MM15 | The corresponding projected strand passage across a saddle band. |

A **distant interchange** exchanges the order of two elementary movie events with disjoint spatial supports, including Reidemeister events and Morse events; it is not restricted to two critical points of the smooth surface-height function. A planar isotopy of a whole movie and the insertion or removal of stationary frames do not count as additional local types. Sweep-around is a separate spherical operation, absent from this Euclidean list.

Fix a based closed disk $D$ and a finite even subset $B\subset\partial D$. A smoothing is a compact smooth one-manifold in $D$, with boundary precisely $B$ and fixed radial collars there; it may contain circles. A morphism from $P$ to $Q$ is a compact orientable, not separately oriented, smooth surface with corners in $D\times[0,1]$, with bottom $P$, top $Q$, side boundary $B\times[0,1]$ and fixed product collars. Identify surfaces by ambient isotopy relative to these boundary collars. Take free abelian morphism groups, compose by stacking, and impose the following relations in every surrounding surface: a sphere component is zero; a torus component may be deleted with factor $2$; and $C_{12}+C_{34}=C_{13}+C_{24}$, where $C_{ij}$ attaches a tube between disk patches $i,j$ among four disjoint patches in a ball. Denote the resulting category by $\mathcal C(B)$.

For a surface $C$ set $\deg C=\chi(C)-|B|/2$. Permit formal shifts $P\{a\}$, with a surface of degree $e$ having degree $e+b-a$ as a map $P\{a\}\to Q\{b\}$. Take finite direct sums with matrices of morphisms. A complex is a bounded cochain complex in this additive category, whose differential has internal degree zero. A chain map has cochain degree zero; all homotopies have cochain degree $-1$. Unless specified otherwise, maps and homotopies have internal degree zero. Two chain maps are homotopic when $f-g=dh+hd$. Write $K(B)$ for the category with these complexes as objects and chain maps modulo homotopy as morphisms. Call a complex simple if its invertible endomorphisms in $K(B)$ of internal degree zero are exactly the two maps $\pm\operatorname{id}$ (allowing coincidence when the object is zero).

A planar template is a disk with finitely many numbered input disks removed and a properly embedded one-manifold of arcs and circles in the remainder, meeting each boundary in its prescribed marked points. It acts on smoothings by insertion, and on surfaces by insertion in the template crossed with $[0,1]$. Extend by multilinearity to finite sums. For ordered complexes $C_1,\ldots,C_s$ its totalization has term $\bigoplus_{r_1+\cdots+r_s=r}D(C_1^{r_1},\ldots,C_s^{r_s})$, with shifts added, and differential $\sum_i(-1)^{r_1+\cdots+r_{i-1}}D(1,\ldots,d_i,\ldots,1)$ on that summand. For homogeneous maps $f_i$ of cochain degrees $a_i$, use the sign $(-1)^{\sum_i a_i\sum_{j<i}r_j}$ on $D(f_1,\ldots,f_s)$, evaluated on the input summand of degrees $(r_j)$; this is the usual tensor sign convention, independently of the internal grading.

derivations.claim: **Inverse clips.** For MM1–MM5, a Reidemeister move is followed by its selected inverse, possibly with a planar change of frame between them. The equations in [F2] make the composite homotopic to the identity. All reflections and compatible strand orientations use the corresponding specified local coordinate identification in [F1]; the cochain and internal shifts agree at both ends. Thus the five inverse clips satisfy their formal movie relation before any closed evaluation.

**Simple base frames for the five circular clips.** Each of MM6–MM10 consists solely of Reidemeister moves, so it gives a degree-zero homotopy automorphism of its starting tangle complex by [F2]. The following explicit starting frames of the models in [F7] are simple. For MM7 choose the frame before the small cusp loop: it is a single bent arc, hence a pairing. For MM8 choose the frame before the cusp crosses the third strand: its two arcs have one transverse crossing and no small loop; peeling this sole boundary crossing leaves a pairing. For MM9 choose the frame before the cubic double-curve turn: it likewise has two arcs with one crossing, which peels off at the boundary. The MM6 starting frame is two parallel arcs crossed by a third transverse arc. Its two crossings peel in order from an end of the transverse arc, leaving three disjoint arcs. More explicitly, the outermost crossing has two adjacent free legs in the disk boundary; cut a small collar rectangle containing that crossing and those legs, leaving one boundary-crossing addition to the smaller tangle. After removing it the other crossing has the same property. For MM10 the initial frame is the four small affine strand segments resolving the projected quadruple point, with six pairwise crossings. Choose a linear height not perpendicular to any segment and place upper and lower cuts beyond all six crossings. Each segment is a graph over that height. Order the six crossing heights after a small planar perturbation; the highest crossing is between adjacent outgoing strands, so its two free legs give a boundary-crossing collar rectangle. Remove it and repeat down the ordered list. This peels all six crossings and leaves a pairing, for every retained over/under order. These cuts merely parametrize the local disk and straighten its outside arcs; no crossing change is used. Thus the boundary-crossing equivalences in [F4] and [F2], beginning with [F3], prove simplicity of all five base frames. Starting the same circular clip at a different frame conjugates its endomorphism by a product of equivalences, so [F4] also gives simplicity there.

**The five Morse clips.** For MM11 use the explicit disk cancellation. For MM12 and MM13 use the two columns $D_a-T,D_b-T$ and the integral identity $D_a+D_b=2T$; the upward clips have their separately checked cap/saddle maps. For MM14 use its two circle-birth columns, with the reverse-order RII cube sign retained in both. For MM15 use the residual saddle column $(\alpha,\beta)^T$, or its actual target-retract row in the upward version, with the middle cube permutation and last-vertex sign. These are exactly the five proved calculations of [F5]. Hence the two formal maps agree up to a single sign for every nonreversible clip as well.

**Circular clips.** The degree-zero homotopy automorphism of each MM6–MM10 base frame is therefore homotopic to $\varepsilon1$, where $\varepsilon=1$ or $-1$. This is one scalar in the formal endomorphism group of the whole local complex, not a separate sign on its states. Changing a base frame conjugates that equation by equivalences and preserves the same assertion. A relation presented as two alternative paths is equivalent to its circular clip: compose one path with the selected inverse of the other; its homotopy inverse exists by [F2]. Multiplying the circular equation by the other path therefore makes the two path maps equal up to this one sign. This proves all five circular relations without assuming that arbitrary maps between two homology groups agree up to sign.

**Outside complexes and distant events.** Insert each formal equation or homotopy into the fixed planar outside by [F4]. For two distant elementary events, decompose their disjoint support disks and the outside as one planar operation. Their maps have cochain degree zero; a Morse map can have nonzero quantum degree, but the totalization signs use cochain degree alone. Acting in the first disk and then the second therefore gives the same matrix as acting in the opposite order. The crossing-order changes in [F1] are exactly the signed tensor interchanges of [F7], so the assertion also holds when a Reidemeister event changes the number or order of crossings. In particular it holds for the two distant surface-height critical events in the statement. Now all objects are closed resolutions. Apply [F6] entry by entry; its additivity, gluing and relation factorization preserve each formal chain-map equality and homotopy. The images are precisely the integral maps fixed in [F1], including empty resolutions and the identity on unaffected circles.

Pass to homology in step 3.1. A chain homotopy becomes equality, and the one scalar $\varepsilon$ becomes multiplication by that same overall sign on the full integral homology group. The construction covered MM1–MM5, MM6–MM10 and MM11–MM15, all their stated variants, and the distant interchanges. Thus every relation asserted in the statement preserves the selected map up to one sign. No assertion about spherical sweep-around follows from these Euclidean local computations.

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets (Finite, countably infinite, countable, uncountable) has a choice function.

Assume countable choice and fix a generic movie $M$ of a smooth oriented surface cobordism $\Sigma$ from an oriented link $L_0$ to an oriented link $L_1$. For each regular frame $D$, let $Kh(D)$ be the normalized integral Khovanov homology group. The empty frame has the one-term complex $\mathbb Z$ in both gradings zero, using the empty resolution and the zero-fold tensor product. Associate to a birth the unit map $\eta:\mathbb Z\to\mathcal A$, $\eta(1)=1$; associate to a death the counit $\epsilon:\mathcal A\to\mathbb Z$, $\epsilon(1)=0,\epsilon(X)=1$; and associate to a saddle the multiplication $m:\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ when two resolution circles merge, or the comultiplication $\Delta:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A$ when one splits. Each local map is tensored with the identity on unaffected circles. Associate to planar isotopy the induced identification of the cube complexes. For Reidemeister moves, use the following fixed Bar-Natan constructions: the kink retractions $F_+=v-\Delta$, $G_+=e$, $F_-=u$, $G_-=w-m$; the two inverse-crossing strong retractions with degree-zero inclusion $(1,ut)^T$ and projection $(1,-se)$, with their specified reverse-order cube signs; and the third-move equivalences obtained by the explicit source- or target-cone retractions onto the common six-point residual complex. Here $u,e$ are circle birth/death, $v,w$ are punctured-torus birth/death, and the saddle letters denote the actual local bands in these constructions. Use their specified inverses for the reversed moves. Insert these formal surface matrices into the fixed planar outside of the diagram, then apply the integral Frobenius cobordism functor. Normalize a state $v$ to cochain degree $|v|-n_-$ and quantum shift $|v|+n_+-2n_-$. Fix the local coordinate identifications and orientation cases once, with the Koszul crossing-order correction $(-1)^{v(a)v(b)}$ when crossings $a,b$ are interchanged. These local maps are chosen once; composing them with an arbitrary automorphism of a complex is not an allowed change of representative. Compose the induced maps on homology in movie order and denote the result by $Kh(M):Kh(L_0)\to Kh(L_1)$, considered modulo multiplication by $-1$. This definition fixes a movie; independence from changing the movie is not included in the definition.

Assume countable choice. For each Carter–Saito movie move, the two movie segments have the same incoming and outgoing oriented link diagrams and represent isotopic portions of an oriented surface cobordism relative to their boundary collars. The induced maps on the integral even Khovanov homology groups of those diagrams differ by multiplication by a single overall sign. The same conclusion holds when two disjoint critical points of the height function are interchanged.

Assume countable choice. Let $\Sigma_0,\Sigma_1\subset S^3\times[0,1]$ be compact smooth properly embedded oriented surfaces from fixed oriented knots $K_0$ to $K_1$, with the same boundary parametrizations and product collars. Suppose their generic movies represent ambient isotopic cobordisms by an isotopy fixed on those collars. Then one movie can be changed to the other by a finite sequence of the fifteen Carter–Saito movie moves, sweep-around moves, and interchanges of two disjoint elementary movie events (including disjoint critical points of the surface-height function). A sweep-around moves a closing arc of a one-interval tangle over the tangle to its other side and back underneath, or reverses that movie; geometrically it is a local sheet passage through the missing vertical arc in a spatial chart $S^3\setminus\{\infty\}$. Every intermediate movie represents a generic surface cobordism with the same fixed boundary data.

Assume countable choice. Let $P$ be a single arc in a disk and let $Z=P\sqcup O$ add a small disjoint circle next to it. Let $m:Z\to P$ merge the circle into the arc by an elementary saddle and let $\Delta:P\to Z$ be the reversed saddle. In the open Bar-Natan category the two normalized kink complexes $C_+=(Z\{1\}\xrightarrow{m}P\{2\})$ in cochain degrees $0,1$, and $C_-=(P\{-2\}\xrightarrow{\Delta}Z\{-1\})$ in degrees $-1,0$, both have explicit internal degree zero strong deformation retractions onto the one-term complex $P$ in degree zero. These retractions are preserved by insertion into an arbitrary planar surrounding complex.

Assume countable choice. In the open Bar-Natan category on four boundary points of a rectangle, let $I$ be the vertical two-strand identity pairing and let $E$ be the pairing consisting of a top cap and bottom cup. Let $t:I\to E$ and $s:E\to I$ be the elementary saddle surfaces. Define the formal crossing complexes $K_+=(I\{1\}\xrightarrow{t}E\{2\})$, in cochain degrees $0,1$, and $K_-=(E\{-2\}\xrightarrow{s}I\{-1\})$, in degrees $-1,0$. Then both planar stackings $K_+K_-$ and $K_-K_+$ have explicit internal degree zero strong deformation retractions onto the one-term complex $I$ in degree zero, with no grading shift. All maps and homotopies can be inserted into an arbitrary planar surrounding complex. Consequently adjoining either of these crossing complexes preserves simplicity in both directions.

Assume countable choice. Put six points on a disk boundary in clockwise order $1,2,3,4,5,6$, at northwest, northeast, east, southeast, southwest and west. Consider diagonal arcs $a$ from $1$ to $4$ and $b$ from $2$ to $5$, and an arc $c$ from $6$ to $3$. In the left diagram $c$ bows above the intersection of $a,b$; in the right it bows below. In both diagrams $c$ passes over both diagonals. Either $a$ passes over $b$ in both diagrams, or $b$ passes over $a$ in both. These are the two local third Reidemeister variants considered here. More precisely one can use the diameters $y=-x,y=x$ for $a,b$ and the curves $y=\pm h(1-x^2)$, $0<h<1/2$, for $c$, with fixed radial collars near the six boundary points.

Use the local smoothing chart in which the over-strand joins southwest to northeast and the under-strand joins northwest to southeast. The A-smoothing joins the left pair and right pair, and the B-smoothing joins the top pair and bottom pair. An A-first cube uses $0=A,1=B$; a B-first cube uses $0=B,1=A$. For either convention, the raw formal cube of an ordered diagram has term $\bigoplus_{|v|=s}S_v\{s\}$ in cochain degree $s$ and edge saddle coefficient $(-1)^{\sum_{k<j}v_k}$ in coordinate $j$. For any choice of strand orientations, put this term in degree $s-n_-$ and shift it internally by the additional $n_+-2n_-$.

For each of these two smoothing conventions, the formal cubes of the two diagrams admit internal degree zero chain homotopy equivalences, with explicit maps given below. The displayed smoothing table and cone calculation use A-first cubes: turning right from an entering underpassing half-line gives the A-smoothing. The B-first maps are obtained from the raw A-first maps by complementing every bit and reversing surface time, without spatial reflection, with the explicit vertex sign correction below; only after this operation are the same given $n_+,n_-$ normalizations applied to both sides. All these maps and homotopies can be inserted into any planar surrounding complex.

In the open Bar-Natan categories, planar totalization defines operations on bounded complexes and on their homotopy categories, preserving internal degrees and homotopy equivalences. Simplicity is invariant under an internal degree zero chain homotopy equivalence. In particular let $A$ and $B$ be the operations of adjoining a fixed boundary crossing complex and its proposed inverse, each using precisely two adjacent boundary legs. Suppose local internal degree zero chain homotopy equivalences of their two possible composites with the straight two-strand identity complex have been supplied. Then a complex $C$ is simple if and only if $A(C)$ is simple. This is a conditional assertion about these local inverse equivalences; it does not assert Reidemeister invariance or provide crossing complexes or their inverse maps.

Assume countable choice. In the open Bar-Natan category, let $P$ be a smoothing consisting of $k$ arcs and no circles, including $k=0$. The map $\mathbb Z\to\operatorname{End}^0(P)$ sending $n$ to $n\operatorname{id}_P$ is an isomorphism of rings. Consequently the one-term complex $P$, with any common grading shift, is simple.

derivations.claim: **A local integral comparison category.** Use oriented blue facets of label $1$ and red facets of label $2$; two blue facets meet a red facet along each seam, with the usual merge orientation. Decorations on blue facets are powers of a dot. One can define their closed evaluation by cutting at the circular seams and applying the two Frobenius algebras $B=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$, $\epsilon_B(1)=0$, $\epsilon_B(X)=1$, $\Delta_B(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1$, $\Delta_B(X)=X\otimes X$, and $R=\mathbb Z$ with counit $-1$ and comultiplication $-1\otimes1$. Contract a seam by $\epsilon_B(x\bar y)$, where the positive blue side is selected by right-hand cyclic order and $\bar X=-X$. Cut-independence is the unit, counit, associativity and Frobenius identities of these displayed algebras. Equivalently, this is the following direct specialization of the two-pigment evaluation. With roots $x_1,x_2$, put $d=x_1-x_2$, $h=x_1+x_2$, $t=-x_1x_2$, and use $B_h=\mathbb Z[h,t][X]/(X^2-hX-t)$. Its primitive idempotents have counits $\beta_1=1/d$, $\beta_2=-1/d$, and conjugation interchanges them. A connected blue facet of genus $g$ with $b$ seam circles contributes $\beta_i^{1-g-b}$; a red facet contributes $(-1)^{1-g-b}$; the seam contributes $\beta_i$ for its positive blue pigment. Sum over the two colors, which must be different at each seam. This is a finite tensor contraction in $B_h$ and $R$, hence is integral before any localization. Define states of a closed web as foams from the empty web modulo the common radical of every closing evaluation; define all other morphisms by bending to a closed web and taking that radical. Gluing preserves the radical because every closing after gluing is a closing before gluing. These definitions provide a local category, with no assertion of full faithfulness for a previously defined homology-valued functor.

**Reduction to an almost braid closure is relative.** A finite one-to-one tangle diagram, possibly with additional closed components, can be braided while preserving a prescribed short crossing-free endpoint arc. Here is the relative finite braiding construction needed, rather than an invocation of an AC-stated existence theorem. Close that arc on the left, choose a generic height away from its small fixed rectangle, and subdivide the remaining finitely many projected arcs at extrema and between changes of over/under status. A backward arc can be replaced by two forward arcs extending past the diagram and the exterior return arc: lift its small triangular detour above the rest when it is over, or below when under, then straighten the two free legs to the height direction. Its attaching intervals stay fixed and its chosen side has no strand between the old and new arc, so sliding across this triangle is an isotopy of the embedded tangle. Subdivision makes every such detour contain at most one old crossing of a fixed status. The detours introduce only forward legs and are chosen away from the fixed endpoint rectangle. Repeating on the finite backward list gives a braid whose rightmost $n$ strands are closed, and whose remaining strand retains the prescribed open endpoints. This is an almost braid closure. All moves occur in compact balls away from the fixed arc; smoothing the finite corners and extending the local velocities gives a relative smooth isotopy and a finite Euclidean movie. By [F2], conjugating a sweep by this isotopy conjugates its projective map. Therefore it suffices to prove the sweep identity for an almost braid closure.

**All actual rank-two foams are covered.** In the positive-label raw foam category a facet of label at least three has no two-pigment coloring. Every closure of a foam containing it therefore evaluates to zero, so that foam is in the radical. Each allowed tetrahedral vertex has such a facet: its first positive-label model contains $a+b+c\ge3$; its second has $a>c\ge1$, $b\ge1$, and contains $a+b\ge3$. Thus every nonzero rank-two foam is vertex-free, with precisely the facets of step 1.1; no zero-facet removal assertion is required. To compare raw left-hand Robert–Wagner signs with the right-hand evaluation above, let $B_i$ be the blue pigment-$i$ surfaces, $R$ the red surface, $M$ the seam count, and $t_i$ the number of seams positive on blue pigment $i$ in right-hand order. Their two sign exponents are $\chi(B_1\cup R)/2+t_2$ and $\chi(B_2\cup R)/2+t_1$. Their difference modulo two is $\chi(B)/2+\chi(R)+M=\chi(B)/2$, since $\chi(R)\equiv M\pmod2$. Their common denominator is $d^{\chi(B)/2}$. Consequently raw evaluation differs by $(-1)^{\chi(B)/2}$. At $h=t=0$ a nonzero scalar evaluation with $D$ blue dots has $2D=\chi(B)$; replacing each raw blue dot by its negative cancels this sign. Positive-degree red decorations specialize to zero. Thus every closed evaluation, and hence every bent radical, agrees after this explicit dot normalization. In particular the normalized dotted sphere is $+1$; it is not identified with the unrenormalized raw dotted sphere, which is $-1$.

**Pairing bases, without red compression.** A closed web with $k$ underlying blue circles has exactly $2^k$ boundary pigment states: a pigment changes across every red vertex on its blue circle, and there are an even number of these vertices because blue orientation changes there. Localized closed evaluation factors through these states, so its pairing rank is at most $2^k$. For a pure-blue web, dotted disk cups and complementary dotted caps have a unimodular tensor-product pairing: the one-circle Gram matrix is $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\1&h\end{smallmatrix}\right)$, of determinant $-1$. Hence its universal module is exactly the free module with those $2^k$ cups. For a general web $W$, there is a foam $I_W$ with underlying blue cylinders from standardly oriented blue circles to $W$. To construct it, checkerboard-color the complement of the underlying blue cylinders; complete every wrongly oriented region boundary by a red copy, push its interior into that region and assign the opposite color in the new thin region. The boundary red arcs are completed in the same way. This finite construction uses only parallel copies in collars, so produces the prescribed boundary and no singular vertices. The reflected composite $I_W^*I_W$ commutes with dots: crossing a seam changes $X$ to $h-X$, and each blue cylinder crosses an even number of orientation changes. It is degree zero, so on the pure-blue module it is multiplication by an integer. For each fixed boundary pigment, its color contraction is a single nonzero term of absolute value one; hence that integer is $\pm1$. Thus $I_W$ has a left inverse. Its cokernel is a direct summand of the universal module, is torsion-free because all its pairing evaluations lie in the domain $\mathbb Z[h,t]$, and has rank zero by the localized $2^k$ bound. It is zero, and $I_W$ is invertible. Bending now identifies every local morphism space with the corresponding blue cup module. In particular a $k$-arc pairing has basis degrees $2|L|$ in its degree-zero endomorphism calculation, so $\operatorname{End}^0=\mathbb Z\,1$. This argument does not compress a possibly knotted red surface in a ball.

**The actual crossing and tensor conventions.** Let $I$ be the two-strand pairing and $A_i$ the thick web at adjacent positions $i,i+1$. In the over-southwest-to-northeast source chart, $I$ is the A-smoothing and the underlying blue pairing of $A_i$ is the B-smoothing. Use auxiliary crossing factors $(A_i\{-1\}\to I)$ in degrees $(-1,0)$ and $(I\to A_i\{1\})$ in degrees $(0,1)$ for the two inverse physical braid generators. These are the two rank-two foam factors with all-parallel term in degree zero; the braces here are the formal shift convention, opposite to their printed $q$ exponent. Surface-time cochain duality, with intrinsic grading changed from $-\chi$ to $\chi$, gives $(I\to E_i\{1\})$ and $(E_i\{-1\}\to I)$, respectively. Assume countable choice. Let $\Sigma\subset S^3\times[0,1]$ be a compact smooth oriented cobordism from an oriented knot $K_0$ to an oriented knot $K_1$, with fixed product collars and fixed endpoint diagrams. Every generic movie $M$ of $\Sigma$ defines a map of bidegree $(0,\chi(\Sigma))$,
$$
Kh(M):Kh^{i,j}(K_0)\longrightarrow Kh^{i,j+\chi(\Sigma)}(K_1),
$$
where $\chi(\Sigma)$ is the Euler characteristic of the surface and the integral even Khovanov groups use the normalized crossing shifts. If two such movies represent cobordisms related by an ambient isotopy fixed on the boundary collars, their maps differ by multiplication by a single overall sign, independent of the input class. The resulting assignment is a functor after each morphism group is quotiented by the relation identifying a map with its negative; before that quotient the sign is not canonical.

Let $(W,\Sigma,\mathcal A)$ be a decorated knot cobordism from $(Y_0,K_0)$ to $(Y_1,K_1)$, and fix $\mathfrak s\in\operatorname{Spin}^c(W)$. Choose a parametrized Kirby decomposition of $W$, together with admissible Heegaard data and regular almost-complex structures for its elementary pieces. Intermediate pieces may contain links with several components or more than one pair of basepoints. Use the colored multipointed modules with $g+n-1$ attaching curves in $\operatorname{Sym}^{g+n-1}(S)$, and specialize all $w$-colors to $U$ and all $z$-colors to $V$; the displayed doubly pointed formula is the $n=1$ case. For a piece represented by a subordinate Heegaard triple $(S,\boldsymbol\alpha,\boldsymbol\beta,\boldsymbol\gamma,w,z)$, its triangle-count map has the form
$$
\mathbf x\longmapsto \sum_{\mathbf y}\ \sum_{\substack{\phi\in\pi_2(\mathbf x,\Theta^+_{\boldsymbol\beta\boldsymbol\gamma},\mathbf y)\\ \mu(\phi)=0,\ \mathfrak s(\phi)=\mathfrak s}} \#_2\bigl(\mathcal M(\phi)\bigr)U^{n_w(\phi)}V^{n_z(\phi)}\mathbf y,
$$
where $\Theta^+_{\boldsymbol\beta\boldsymbol\gamma}$ denotes a chosen cycle representative of the distinguished top-degree homology class of the appropriate standard auxiliary Heegaard pair, $\mathfrak s(\phi)$ is the Spin-c structure determined by the triangle class, and the other symbols and coefficient ring are as in the two-color target definition. For a chosen auxiliary cycle with finite support $\Theta=\sum_j p_j\theta_j$, with $p_j\in\mathbb F_2[U,V]$ and basis generators $\theta_j$, interpret the displayed formula by $\mathbb F_2[U,V]$-linearity as $\sum_j p_j F(\mathbf x,\theta_j)$ (or $\sum_j p_j F(\theta_j,\mathbf x)$ for the alpha-triple convention). The elementary 2-handle maps and band maps are triangle-count maps; the 0-, 1-, 3-, and 4-handle maps use the corresponding stabilization or destabilization maps; cylindrical changes of the dividing set use basepoint and quasi-stabilization maps. Compose the elementary maps in the chosen decomposition to obtain a representative
$$
\widetilde F_{W,\Sigma,\mathcal A,\mathfrak s,\mathcal K}: CFL^-_{UV}(Y_0,K_0,\mathfrak s|_{Y_0})\longrightarrow CFL^-_{UV}(Y_1,K_1,\mathfrak s|_{Y_1}).
$$
The subscript $\mathcal K$ records the chosen decomposition and auxiliary data. This is one map for one Spin-c structure; maps for different Spin-c structures are not summed unless a sum is explicitly specified. Independence from $\mathcal K$, regular data, and parametrization is a separate naturality assertion.

Let $(W,\Sigma,\mathcal A)$ be a decorated knot cobordism between doubly pointed knots in $S^3$, and let $\mathfrak s\in\operatorname{Spin}^c(W)$. The representative maps from any two parametrized Kirby decompositions and admissible regular Heegaard choices are filtered $\mathbb F_2[U,V]$-equivariantly chain homotopic. If the decorated cobordism is a composite of $(W_1,\Sigma_1,\mathcal A_1)$ followed by $(W_2,\Sigma_2,\mathcal A_2)$, then for fixed Spin-c structures $\mathfrak s_i$ on $W_i$,
$$
\widetilde F_{W_2,\Sigma_2,\mathcal A_2,\mathfrak s_2}\circ \widetilde F_{W_1,\Sigma_1,\mathcal A_1,\mathfrak s_1} \simeq \sum_{\substack{\mathfrak s\in\operatorname{Spin}^c(W)\\ \mathfrak s|_{W_i}=\mathfrak s_i,\ i=1,2}} \widetilde F_{W,\Sigma,\mathcal A,\mathfrak s}.
$$
The sum is over Spin-c structures on the glued cobordism restricting to the specified structures on the two pieces. For $W=S^3\times[0,1]$, $\operatorname{Spin}^c(W)$ has one element, so the sum has one term and the composition law is ordinary composition up to filtered equivariant chain homotopy.

Let $D$ be a nonempty finite regular oriented link diagram in an oriented $3$-sphere, with finite crossing set $C(D)$. Fix a unit viewing normal $n$ and orient the projection plane $P$ so $(u,v)$ is positive exactly when $(n,u,v)$ is positive in the ambient $3$-space. At a crossing $c$, define its sign as the sign of $\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})$, where the two nonzero projected tangent vectors follow the oriented over- and under-strands. Let $n_+$ and $n_-$ be the numbers of positive and negative crossings.

Set $\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$, with $\deg(1)=1$ and $\deg(X)=-1$. Its unit, multiplication, counit, and comultiplication are
$$
\eta(1)=1,\qquad m(1\otimes1)=1,\quad m(1\otimes X)=m(X\otimes1)=X,\quad m(X\otimes X)=0,
$$
$$
\epsilon(1)=0,\quad\epsilon(X)=1,\qquad \Delta(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1,\quad\Delta(X)=X\otimes X.
$$
Thus $m$ and $\Delta$ have quantum degree $-1$, while $\eta$ and $\epsilon$ have degree $+1$.

Choose a total order $c_1<\cdots<c_n$ on $C(D)$. A resolution state is a function $v:C(D)\to\{0,1\}$; at $v(c)=0$ use the A-smoothing and at $v(c)=1$ use the B-smoothing from the Kauffman source chart. Write $|v|=\sum_c v(c)$, let $D_v$ be the crossingless resolution, and let $k(v)$ be its number of circles. Assign the state module $\mathcal A^{\otimes k(v)}$. For an edge $v\to v+e_j$ changing crossing $c_j$ from $0$ to $1$, use $m$ if the local smoothing merges two circles and $\Delta$ if it splits one circle, tensored with the identity on all other factors, and multiply this map by $(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}v(c_i)}$. The resulting direct sum has cohomological degree
$$i(v)=|v|-n_-$$
and the generator with circle labels $1$ or $X$ has quantum degree
$$j(v)=|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum_{\text{circle labels }a}\deg(a).$$
This defines the normalized integral Khovanov cube and its candidate degree-zero cochain differential; the assertion that the differential squares to zero is a separate lemma.

The Frobenius identity that controls a merge-split face is represented by the two equal composites below. The diagram records the maps only; the proof verifies the equality on the basis $\{1,X\}^{\otimes2}$ and does not rely on the drawing.

```tikzcd
\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A \arrow[r,"m"] \arrow[d,"\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id}"'] & \mathcal A \arrow[d,"\Delta"] \\
\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A \arrow[r,"\mathrm{id}\otimes m"'] & \mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A
```

derivations.claim: On the basis element $1$, $(\operatorname{id}\otimes\eta)(1)=1\otimes1$, so $m(\operatorname{id}\otimes\eta)(1)=m(1\otimes1)=1$. On the basis element $X$, $(\operatorname{id}\otimes\eta)(X)=X\otimes1$, so $m(\operatorname{id}\otimes\eta)(X)=m(X\otimes1)=X$.

The two basis elements generate $\mathcal A$ as an abelian group, and both are fixed by the composite in step 1.1. By linearity the composite fixes every element of $\mathcal A$, hence equals $\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal A}$.

citations.quote:
Let $D$ be a nonempty finite regular oriented link diagram in an oriented $3$-sphere, with finite crossing set $C(D)$. Fix a unit viewing normal $n$ and orient the projection plane $P$ so $(u,v)$ is positive exactly when $(n,u,v)$ is positive in the ambient $3$-space. At a crossing $c$, define its sign as the sign of $\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})$, where the two nonzero projected tangent vectors follow the oriented over- and under-strands. Let $n_+$ and $n_-$ be the numbers of positive and negative crossings.

Set $\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$, with $\deg(1)=1$ and $\deg(X)=-1$. Its unit, multiplication, counit, and comultiplication are
$$
\eta(1)=1,\qquad m(1\otimes1)=1,\quad m(1\otimes X)=m(X\otimes1)=X,\quad m(X\otimes X)=0,
$$
$$
\epsilon(1)=0,\quad\epsilon(X)=1,\qquad \Delta(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1,\quad\Delta(X)=X\otimes X.
$$
Thus $m$ and $\Delta$ have quantum degree $-1$, while $\eta$ and $\epsilon$ have degree $+1$.

Choose a total order $c_1<\cdots<c_n$ on $C(D)$. A resolution state is a function $v:C(D)\to\{0,1\}$; at $v(c)=0$ use the A-smoothing and at $v(c)=1$ use the B-smoothing from the Kauffman source chart. Write $|v|=\sum_c v(c)$, let $D_v$ be the crossingless resolution, and let $k(v)$ be its number of circles. Assign the state module $\mathcal A^{\otimes k(v)}$. For an edge $v\to v+e_j$ changing crossing $c_j$ from $0$ to $1$, use $m$ if the local smoothing merges two circles and $\Delta$ if it splits one circle, tensored with the identity on all other factors, and multiply this map by $(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}v(c_i)}$. The resulting direct sum has cohomological degree
$$i(v)=|v|-n_-$$
and the generator with circle labels $1$ or $X$ has quantum degree
$$j(v)=|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum_{\text{circle labels }a}\deg(a).$$
This defines the normalized integral Khovanov cube and its candidate degree-zero cochain differential; the assertion that the differential squares to zero is a separate lemma.

The Frobenius identity that controls a merge-split face is represented by the two equal composites below. The diagram records the maps only; the proof verifies the equality on the basis $\{1,X\}^{\otimes2}$ and does not rely on the drawing.

```tikzcd
\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A \arrow[r,"m"] \arrow[d,"\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id}"'] & \mathcal A \arrow[d,"\Delta"] \\
\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A \arrow[r,"\mathrm{id}\otimes m"'] & \mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A
```

derivations.claim: The birth map sends $1\in\mathbb Z$ to $1\in\mathcal A$, and the following death sends this element to $\epsilon(1)=0$. Thus $\epsilon\eta=0:\mathbb Z\to\mathbb Z$.

Tensoring the zero map $\epsilon\eta$ with $\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal A}$ gives the zero endomorphism of $\mathcal A$, which is the composite in the statement. The identity of $\mathcal A$ is nonzero because it sends $1$ to $1\neq0$; its negative also sends $1$ to $-1\neq0$. Hence the composite is neither the identity nor its negative.
